actions.name: target and compromise users using Zimbra Collaboration Suite
actions.description: A group of Russian state-supported cyber actors has been targeting and compromising various Western government and commercial organizations using the Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) software since at least July 2025.
actions.reproducibility_reason: The target host has no deployable service, so it is left out of deployment; this step is not reproduced until a service or substitute is supplied for that host.

actions.name: send email containing malicious JavaScript payload exploiting CVE-2025-66376
actions.description: LAUNDRY BEAR sends an email containing a malicious JavaScript payload to the target. Through exploitation of CVE-2025-66376, this JavaScript payload is immediately executed once the user views the malicious email in the ZCS webmail platform.
actions.reproducibility_reason: The target host has no deployable service, so it is left out of deployment; this step is not reproduced until a service or substitute is supplied for that host.

actions.name: send phishing emails from victim infrastructure through compromised accounts
actions.description: Since at least November 2025, LAUNDRY BEAR began sending these phishing emails from victim infrastructure through compromised accounts to obfuscate and frustrate anti-phishing tools and training.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Catalogue has no exact component/version and safe validation mapping for this action; provide the target software, version, and expected evidence.

actions.name: execute JavaScript payload exploiting zero-day vulnerability CVE-2025-66376
actions.description: The JavaScript payload included in the malicious email exploits CVE-2025-66376, a zero-day vulnerability at the time of initial exploitation, allowing execution of arbitrary JavaScript when the email is viewed.
actions.reproducibility_reason: The target host has no deployable service, so it is left out of deployment; this step is not reproduced until a service or substitute is supplied for that host.

actions.name: collect victim information in 12 asynchronous stages
actions.description: The malicious JavaScript payload attempts to collect and exfiltrate victim information in 12 asynchronous stages including email address, environment data, 2FA codes, application passwords, device status, OAuth consumers, autocomplete passwords, mail protocol enabling, Global Address List, and email archives.
actions.reproducibility_reason: The target host has no deployable service, so it is left out of deployment; this step is not reproduced until a service or substitute is supplied for that host.

actions.name: establish persistence by modifying account preferences and collecting authentication information
actions.description: The script attempts to establish sustained persistence into the victim’s email account by modifying account preferences such as enabling IMAP, creating Application Passcodes, and collecting 2FA tokens.
actions.reproducibility_reason: The target host has no deployable service, so it is left out of deployment; this step is not reproduced until a service or substitute is supplied for that host.

actions.name: exfiltrate collected data via DNS and HTTPS to Flowerbed infrastructure
actions.description: The script exfiltrates collected victim information using DNS A record queries and HTTPS POST requests to actor-controlled Flowerbed infrastructure, employing Base32 encoding for DNS and encrypted HTTPS with valid certificates.
actions.reproducibility_reason: The target host has no deployable service, so it is left out of deployment; this step is not reproduced until a service or substitute is supplied for that host.

actions.name: use compromised accounts to send phishing emails
actions.description: LAUNDRY BEAR uses previously compromised victim accounts to send phishing emails containing the malicious payload, to obfuscate and frustrate anti-phishing tools and training.
